newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Tycoon seen heading Indonesia's Astra.
newsitem.headline: Tycoon seen heading Indonesia's Astra.

text.p: Business tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan, a close associate of Indonesia's President Suharto, is tipped to take a key role in the country's largest carmaker, PT Astra International, brokers and analysts said on Tuesday.
Brokers said there was intense market talk that Hasan would be appointed chief commissioner of Astra, maker of the nation's most popular Kijang car, at the company's EGM on Wednesday.
"It is widely believed that Hasan is the strongest candidate for commissioner," a broker with a Japanese securities firm said.

But he said the speculation on changes in Astra's board of commissioners was no longer affecting sentiment in shares of the firm, which dominates the local car market with the Toyota, Daihatsu, Isuzu, BMW, Peugeot and Nissan brands.
Astra also makes Honda motorcycles.
"It is a sound company which is doing very well and so far it's a widely held public company in Indonesia. The changes, I believe, will not have much impact on its bottom line," the broker said.

But brokers said the market would be more interested in changes in the company's day-to-day management as there was speculation that the current president director, Theodore Permadi Rachmat, had decided to step down.
"I have heard that finance director Rini Suwandi is the strongest candidate for president director," a broker said.
If Suwandi, who has headed Astra's corporate finance department since 1990, rose to the top job, she would be one of few Indonesian woman to head a major listed company.
David O'Neil, analyst of BZW Niaga Securities, said changes in Astra's board of commissioners could add value to the firm.
"In terms of earnings growth, Astra will do superbly well for the next three or four years," O'Neil said.
But he added that while it might be difficult for the board of commissioners to directly enhance the earnings growth they could play a key role in business development.

"There will be discussions on business development such as Astra's wood-based industries, its non-core assets and also the flotation of its subsidiaries on which I am sure they are going to have a view on those issues," he added.
On Tuesday, Bisnis Indonesia newspaper quoted Hasan as saying it was up to the majority shareholders to appoint Astra's commissioners.
Hasan said in future Astra should be developed in such a way as to give benefit to Indonesia in general.
"For automotive industry, we will increase the use of local components and boost exports," he was quoted as saying.
The extraordinary general meeting is the first since major changes in Astra International's ownership late last year.
Hasan's Nusamba group now holds 10 percent of Astra's stock, the largest single stake in the company. Nusamba is 80 percent owned by charitable foundations headed by President Suharto.
Hasan and the president's eldest son, Sigit Hardjojudanto, each own a 10 percent stake in Nusamba.

Hasan chaired the so-called "new investors consortium" in Astra that includes Anthony Salim of the diversified Salim Group, cigarette maker Putera Sampoerna, timber tycoon Projogo Pangestu and Usman Admadjaja of Danamon International.
The five men hold more than 50 percent of Astra, in which Toyota Motor Co of Japan has an 8.26 percent stake.

Hasan, through Nusamba group, holds a controlling interest of just over 50 percent in PT Askatindo Karya Mineral and PT Amsya Lina which are involved in the giant Busang gold project in East Kalimantan.
